report:
Reviewed the complete storage claim and the complete associated test set. Requirements are (1) distinct source-CST and result stashes, (2) checked types, binders, predicates and retained aliases owned by the result, and (3) independence from parser/tree-sitter and source-CST borrows. Check::new borrows source_stash but creates a new target_stash; finish consumes Check and moves that target into Stashed. Stashed owns its arena and root, with no source-stash reference. Added ordinary associations for the essential lowering and copying files, then restarted this review against the updated inputs. TypeCst::check recursively reads source nodes and allocates reference, slice, array, tuple, and function children in the target; primitive/error/parameter leaves are semantic values. PathSegment::check_type_args allocates even the empty argument list in the target. resolution_to_ty retains named aliases as semantic definition identity plus that checked argument list, not CST handles. CheckGenerics constructs semantic generic symbols and allocates their slice in the target. lower_predicates allocates subject types, trait argument lists, and predicate slices in the target; Check::complete_parameter_env assembles only target-owned clauses. Local function signature construction allocates parameter/return types, binder generic lists, and combined environments in the target; open_owner uses Stashed::copy_into before exposing owner self types and predicates. StashCopy recursively copies Ptr and Slice contents, so ownership is not a shallow handle copy. External ADT application places defaults and completed argument lists in its supplied target; Substitute/default_fold_ty and fold_parameter_env recursively map pointer-bearing types, alias forms, trait references and predicates from the external signature stash into that target. No tree-sitter value is used by these checked-result constructors. Database-scoped symbol identities are retained as semantic identities; the claim does not require detachment from the database. All nine ordinary implementation entries are accounted for: check/sig, check/trait_env, cst/generics, cst/paths, cst/ty, external_syms, local_syms/fns, ty_fold, and sage-stash.
The sole associated test, sage_meta::todo::checking_signature_storage, has an empty body and no assertions. It explicitly defers the required structural traversal matrix after source/parser borrows end, including retained aliases and predicates and cross-stash-pointer detection. This is accepted as a visible test deferral, not evidence that runtime ownership has been verified. Its prerequisite is implementing those representative signature fixtures and traversals; existing debug stash identity checks make indexed cross-stash access observable, but this review does not claim the placeholder exercises them. No N/A entries exist. A shallow copied alias argument or predicate handle would require that deferred matrix to detect the regression.
Validation performed here was source inspection plus cargo meta review start/read and cargo fmt after association-only comments. No behavioral test was executed or asserted to pass by this reviewer. Workspace build and delegated post-codegen/sanity checks are coordinated centrally. No production behavior changed and no behavioral violation was identified.
